clips.text: AI can make a mystery endlessly replayable, but it also makes things up, and a mystery that contradicts itself isn't fair. Roomscript splits the job: an engine proves the case, and the AI only plays the suspects.
You place the case in your room. In the Lens Studio Preview this is a simulated room; the kettle, lamp and desk become the evidence.
Every suspect has a baseline, and a tell. Watch where Vale looks.
That answer was live AI. But it was only allowed to say what the engine handed it, and it was checked before she spoke.
Objects remember. The kettle never boiled.
Break one lie and she retreats to the next. A witness statement breaks that one.
Like Clue, you can test a theory. The other suspects refute it, privately.
Under the hood, truth is compiled, not generated. A solver proves one unique answer
And it was built by coding agents: Codex and Claude Code, using Snap's CLAD skills and the Lens Studio MCP
